inputs.goal: Discover the Kubernetes cluster resources, deploy a MiniCluster of the same number of nodes and maximum cores available. Use the container ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax and target run lmp -v x X -v y Y -v z Z -in in.reaxff.hns, where X Y and Z describe the problem size. It is up to you maximize the Figure of merit, k-atom or M-atom steps/s on one node. You MUST keep increasing X Y Z until the job does not complete or errors. If the run is successful, parse the log and get the FOM. If not, keep trying to deploy until it is fixed. Keep going until you deem optimized and return all FOMs you have parsed.

outputs.data:
GROUP:      flux-framework.org
KIND:       MiniCluster
VERSION:    v1alpha2

FIELD: spec <Object>


DESCRIPTION:
    MiniCluster is an HPC cluster in Kubernetes you can control
    Either to submit a single job (and go away) or for a persistent single- or
    multi- user cluster
    
FIELDS:
  archive	<Object>
    Archive to load or save

  backoffLimit	<integer>
    BackoffLimit is the number of retries for the job before failing

  cleanup	<boolean>
    Cleanup the pods and storage when the index broker pod is complete

  containers	<[]Object> -required-
    Containers is one or more containers to be created in a pod.
    There should only be one container to run flux with runFlux

  deadlineSeconds	<integer>
    Should the job be limited to a particular number of seconds?
    Approximately one year. This cannot be zero or job won't start

  flux	<Object>
    Flux options for the broker, shared across cluster

  interactive	<boolean>
    Run a single-user, interactive minicluster

  jobLabels	<map[string]string>
    Labels for the job

  logging	<Object>
    Logging modes determine the output you see in the job log

  maxSize	<integer>
    MaxSize (maximum number of pods to allow scaling to)

  minSize	<integer>
    MinSize (minimum number of pods that must be up for Flux)
    Note that this option does not edit the number of tasks,
    so a job could run with fewer (and then not start)

  network	<Object>
    A spec for exposing or defining the cluster headless service

  pod	<Object>
    Pod spec details

  services	<[]Object>
    Services are one or more service containers to bring up
    alongside the MiniCluster.

  shareProcessNamespace	<boolean>
    Share process namespace?

  size	<integer>
    Size (number of job pods to run, size of minicluster in pods)
    This is also the minimum number required to start Flux

  tasks	<integer>
    Total number of CPUs being run across entire cluster

# Now prepare to copy finished spack view over
echo "Moving content from /opt/view to be in shared volume at $viewroot"
# Note that /opt/view is a symlink to here!
view=$(ls /opt/views/._view/)
view="/opt/views/._view/${view}"

# Give a little extra wait time
# sleep 10

# We have to move both of these paths, *sigh*
cp -R ${view}/* $viewroot/view
cp -R /opt/software $viewroot/


# This is a marker to indicate the copy is done
touch $viewroot/flux-operator-done.txt
echo "Application is done."
 wait-0:#!/bin/sh

# If we are not in strict, don't set strict mode


# We use the actual time command and not the wrapper, otherwise we get there is no argument -f


# Set the flux user and id from the getgo
fluxuser=$(whoami)
fluxuid=$(id -u $fluxuser)

# If any initCommand logic is defined
 

# Shared logic to wait for view
# We include the view even for disabling flux because it generates needed config files



# Ensure spack view is on the path, wherever it is mounted
viewbase="/mnt/flux"
viewroot=${viewbase}/view
configroot=${viewbase}/config
software="${viewbase}/software"
viewbin="${viewroot}/bin"
fluxpath=${viewbin}/flux

# Set the flux root, don't show the viewer if view is disabled (can be confusing)
# The view is used to have configs and that is it

echo
echo "Flux install root: ${viewroot}"
echo


# Important to add AFTER in case software in container duplicated
export PATH=$PATH:${viewbin}

# Copy mount software to /opt/software
# If /opt/software already exists, we need to copy into it
if [[ -e  "/opt/software" ]]; then
  cp -R ${viewbase}/software/* /opt/software/ || true
else
  cp -R ${viewbase}/software /opt/software || true
fi


foundroot=$(find $viewroot -maxdepth 2 -type d -path $viewroot/lib/python3\*) 
pythonversion=$(basename ${foundroot})
pythonversion=${viewroot}/bin/${pythonversion}
echo "Python version: $pythonversion" 
echo "Python root: $foundroot" 

# Fallback to faux home
if [[ "$HOME" == "/" ]]
  then
    export HOME=/home/flux-operator
    export USER=flux-operator
fi

# If we found the right python, ensure it's linked (old link does not work)
if [[ -f "${pythonversion}" ]]; then
   rm -rf $viewroot/bin/python3
   rm -rf $viewroot/bin/python
   ln -s ${pythonversion} $viewroot/lib/python  || true
   ln -s ${pythonversion} $viewroot/lib/python3 || true
fi

# Ensure we use flux's python (TODO update this to use variable)
export PYTHONPATH=${PYTHONPATH:-""}:${foundroot}/site-packages
echo "PYTHONPATH is ${PYTHONPATH}" 
echo "PATH is $PATH" 

find $viewroot . -name libpython*.so* 
ls -l /mnt/flux/view/lib/libpython3.11.so.1.0 
export FLUX_RC_EXTRA=$viewroot/etc/flux/rc1.d

# Write a script to load fluxion
cat <<EOT >> /tmp/load-fluxion.sh
flux module remove sched-simple
flux module load sched-fluxion-resource
flux module load sched-fluxion-qmanager
EOT
mv /tmp/load-fluxion.sh ${viewbase}/load-fluxion.sh

# Write an easy file we can source for the environment
cat <<EOT >> /tmp/flux-view.sh
#!/bin/bash
export PATH=$PATH
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-""}:$viewroot/lib
export fluxsocket=local://${configroot}/run/flux/local
EOT

# Extra environment added by user (can override above)


mv /tmp/flux-view.sh ${viewbase}/flux-view.sh

# The same, but also connect
cat <<EOT >> /tmp/flux-connect.sh
#!/bin/bash
. \${viewbase}/flux-view.sh
flux proxy \${fluxsocket} bash
EOT
mv /tmp/flux-connect.sh ${viewbase}/flux-connect.sh




# Variables we can use again
cfg="${configroot}/etc/flux/config"
command="lmp -v x 10 -v y 10 -v z 10 -in in.reaxff.hns"

# Is a custom script provided? This will override command





echo 
echo "Hello user ${fluxuser}"
		
# Ensure the flux user owns the curve.cert
# We need to move the curve.cert because config map volume is read only
curvesrc=/flux_operator/curve.cert
curvepath=$configroot/curve/curve.cert

# Prepare curve certificate!
mkdir -p $configroot/curve
cp $curvesrc $curvepath

echo 
echo "🌟️ Curve Certificate"
ls $configroot/curve
cat ${curvepath}


# Remove group and other read
chmod o-r ${curvepath}
chmod g-r ${curvepath}
chown -R ${fluxuid} ${curvepath}

hosts=$(cat ${configroot}/etc/flux/system/hostlist)

echo
echo "📦 Resources"
echo "flux R encode --hosts=${hosts} --local"

flux R encode --hosts=${hosts} --local > /tmp/R
mv /tmp/R ${configroot}/etc/flux/system/R
cat ${configroot}/etc/flux/system/R

# Put the state directory in /var/lib on shared view
export STATE_DIR=${configroot}/var/lib/flux
export FLUX_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/fluxout
mkdir -p ${STATE_DIR} ${FLUX_OUTPUT_DIR}

# Main host <name>-0 and the fully qualified domain name
mainHost="flux-sample-3-0"
workdir=$(pwd)


echo "👋 Hello, I'm $(hostname)"
echo "The main host is ${mainHost}"

echo "The working directory is ${workdir}, contents include:"
ls .


# Make cron.d directory
mkdir -p ${configroot}/etc/flux/system/cron.d
brokerOptions="-Scron.directory=${configroot}/etc/flux/system/cron.d \
  -Stbon.fanout=256 \
  -Srundir=${configroot}/run/flux  \
  -Sstatedir=${STATE_DIR} -Slocal-uri=local://$configroot/run/flux/local \
-Stbon.connect_timeout=5s  \
 \
 \
 -Slog-stderr-level=6  \
  -Slog-stderr-mode=local"


# Run an interactive cluster, giving no command to flux start
function run_interactive_cluster() {
    echo "🌀 flux broker --config-path ${cfg} ${brokerOptions}"
    flux broker --config-path ${cfg} ${brokerOptions}
}

# if we are given an archive to use, load first, not required to exist
# Note that we ask the user to dump in interactive mode - I am not
# sure that doing it with a hook ensures the dump will be successful.


# And pre command logic that isn't passed to the certificate generator
 

# Flux option flags
echo "🚩️ Flux Option Flags defined"

# Start flux with the original entrypoint
if [ $(hostname) == "${mainHost}" ]; then
    
    # If it's a batch job, we write the script for the broker to run
    

    # Commands only run by the broker
     

    echo "Command provided is: ${command}" 
    if [ "${command}" == "" ]; then

       # An interactive job also doesn't require a command
       run_interactive_cluster

    else
    
      # If we are running a batch job, no launcher mode
       # else for if container.batch
         # if tasks >= size
        # Container launchers are snakemake, nextflow, that will launch their own jobs
        
        

# If tasks are == 0, then only define nodes
node_spec="-N 1 -n4"
node_spec="${node_spec}"
flags="${node_spec}  "
echo "Flags for flux are ${flags}" 

        printf "\n🌀 Submit Mode: flux start -o --config ${cfg} ${brokerOptions}  flux submit  ${flags} --quiet --watch ${command}\n"
        
      

      
      

# If tasks are == 0, then only define nodes
node_spec="-N 1 -n4"
node_spec="${node_spec}"
flags="${node_spec}  "
echo "Flags for flux are ${flags}" 

      flux start  -o --config ${cfg} ${brokerOptions}   flux submit  ${flags} --quiet --watch ${command}
       # end if container.launcher
       # end if container.batch
    fi

# Block run by workers
else

   # Commands only run by the workers
    

    # We basically sleep/wait until the lead broker is ready
    echo "🌀 flux start  -o --config ${configroot}/etc/flux/config ${brokerOptions}"

    # We can keep trying forever, don't care if worker is successful or not
    # Unless retry count is set, in which case we stop after retries
    while true
    do
        flux start -o --config ${configroot}/etc/flux/config ${brokerOptions}
        retval=$?
        if [[ "${retval}" -eq 0 ]] || [[ "false" == "true" ]]; then
             echo "The follower worker exited cleanly. Goodbye!"
             break
        fi
        echo "Return value for follower worker is ${retval}"
        echo "😪 Sleeping 15s to try again..."
        sleep 15
    done
fi



# Marker for flux view provider to clean up (within 10 seconds)
touch $viewbase/flux-operator-complete.txt
]
